title: Officers who shot and killed man cleared of wrongdoing: [FINAL C Edition]
article: Two Vancouver police officers who shot a man to death as he sat in a parked stolen car did nothing wrong, B.C.'s police complaints commissioner has concluded.

Thomas Evon Stevenson, 46, was shot at least five times after the officers approached the car parked on East Pender Street and thought Stevenson had reached for a gun. A plastic toy gun was later found near the car.

The Nelson police department investigated the December 2002 shooting and determined the officers acted appropriately and shouldn't face any disciplinary action under the B.C. Police Act. Vancouver Police Chief Jamie Graham agreed.
Bruce Brown, spokesman for the Office of the Police Complaints Commissioner, said the commission reviewed the external police investigation and came to the same conclusion.
"We did our own review of the investigation and agreed with the findings of the external investigation," Brown said yesterday.
He said the family has not requested a public hearing.
Stevenson's family has launched a lawsuit against the Vancouver police. The family's lawyer, Cameron Ward, was unavailable for comment yesterday.
